_status: DRAFT for Tanvir's approval. Not wired into the game. Hotspot positions are placeholders until the Chapter 3 scene exists. Supplies, rules and the rescue are from the spec; all wording is new.
title: Monsoon Leak
opening: Rain. The roof is dripping onto the shelves. I have to save what I can.

intro.p: Three days of rain. Overnight, a corner of the workshop roof gave way.

talk: Laila beta! Your roof is dripping on the lane. Is everything all right in there?
Not really. Water got onto the shelves and the whole batch on the bench has gone stiff and grainy.
No. The roof did. A few drops were enough to ruin it.
Then first, move everything else out of the wet. Dadu must have labelled his shelves.
He did. I will read the labels before I move anything.

lines.text: Before the rains, put every supply in its place. [[torn:…read the label on each shelf…]]
If a batch seizes, do not fight it. [[q:Seized chocolate never becomes a bar again.]]
Stir in hot milk. [[blur:How much?]] Too little stays gritty. Too much turns to water.
lines.note: about as much milk as chocolate

lines.text: Whisk it till it is smooth and glossy, then pour it for the neighbours.

clues.title: The dry shelf label
clues.text: Dadu's handwriting: "Dry shelf. For anything that soaks up water."

clues.title: The sealed jar label
clues.text: "Sealed jar. For anything that takes on smells."

clues.title: Dadu's note on seizing
clues.text: "A few drops of water and chocolate seizes: stiff, grainy, finished as a bar. Do not fight it. Turn it into a drink."

clues.title: Dadu's drinking chocolate note
clues.text: "Hot milk, about as much as the chocolate. Less stays gritty, more makes it thin."

provides.ch3.milk_amount: about as much as the chocolate

clues.title: The bucket under the leak
clues.text: It filled up twice in the night. The sound of the drips kept Laila awake.

steps.title: Line 1: save the supplies
steps.prompt: Tap a supply, then tap the shelf it belongs on. Or drag it there. The labels on each shelf tell you the rule.
steps.say: Six supplies and three shelves. Each shelf has a label in Dadu's handwriting.

items.name: Sugar
items.says: Sugar. It drinks water from the air, and clumps.

items.name: Milk powder
items.says: Milk powder. It goes hard and lumpy if it gets damp.

items.name: Finished bars
items.says: Finished bars. They go soft and dull if they get warm.

items.name: Cocoa butter
items.says: Cocoa butter. It melts at a gentle warmth.

items.name: Roasted nibs
items.says: Roasted nibs. They pick up any smell nearby.

items.name: Cardamom
items.says: Cardamom. A strong smell that can leak into other things.

params.idleInfo: Tap a supply to find out about it.
params.pickFirst: Pick a supply first, then tap a shelf.

feedback.complete: Everything is in its place. Now the batch on the bench.

hints: Read the label on each shelf in the Workshop. Each one says what it is for.
Sugar and milk powder soak up water, so they go on the dry shelf. Bars and cocoa butter melt, so they go on the cool shelf. Roasted nibs and cardamom take on smells, so they go in the sealed jar.

steps.title: Line 2: the seized batch
steps.prompt: The batch on the bench is stiff and grainy. Pick what to do with it.
steps.say: I cannot make a bar out of this. Dadu wrote something about seizing.

options.sense: Add a splash of cold water to loosen it. It looks tempting.
options.no: Cold water only makes it stiffer. A few drops is how it seized in the first place.

options.sense: Melt it and temper it again, the way you would a dark bar.
options.no: It will not come back. It melts into a grainy paste and never sets glossy.

options.sense: Press it into the moulds as it is.
options.no: You would get a crumbly, dull bar that nobody wants. Seized chocolate cannot become a bar again.

options.sense: Stir in hot milk and make it a drink.

params.idleSense: Tap an option to read it.

feedback.correct: Hot milk. If it cannot be a bar, it can still be something warm for the neighbours.

hints: Dadu left a note about what to do when chocolate seizes. Look in the Workshop.
Seized chocolate cannot become a bar, so stir in hot milk and make a drink.

steps.title: Line 3: how much milk?
steps.prompt: Dadu's page is smudged. How much hot milk should go in?
steps.say: Too little and it stays gritty. Too much and it turns to water.

options.no: That is still a stiff paste. It needs more milk to turn into a drink.

options.tag: about as much as the chocolate
options.sense: About as much hot milk as there is chocolate.
The whole pot of hot milk.
options.no: That is thin and watery. The chocolate taste is lost.

params.idleSense: Tap a pour to picture it.

feedback.correct: Smooth and rich. It tastes like the chocolate, only warm.

hints: Dadu's drinking chocolate note says how much. Find it in the Workshop.
About as much hot milk as there is chocolate.

steps.title: Last line: whisk
steps.prompt: Whisk it till it is smooth. Tap the whisk ten times.
steps.say: Whisk it till there are no lumps left.

feedback.correct: Smooth and glossy. Time to pour it for the neighbours.

talk: "Hot chocolate in the rain. Dadu would be proud of you, beta."
It is warm all the way down!
A ruined batch, and I still made something good from it.
recipe: Dry things on the dry shelf, melting things on the cool shelf
Smelly things in the sealed jar
Seized chocolate cannot be a bar
Stir in hot milk, about as much as the chocolate
Whisk till smooth and pour for the neighbours
reveal.realFact: In real life, a few drops of water can make melted chocolate seize. Stir in a lot of liquid and it turns into a sauce or a drink instead.
